paragraphs: Friend, this passage is a revolving door of crowns. In Israel, king after king does evil in the sight of the LORD, and the throne changes hands by conspiracy again and again (2 Kings 15:10, 14, 25, 30). Menahem even pays Assyria a thousand talents of silver to strengthen his own grip on the kingdom (2 Kings 15:19). Look at all that gripping, because Israel's kings keep reaching for their own hold on the crown instead of turning away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat (2 Kings 15:9, 18, 24, 28).

But look at what the LORD keeps doing in the middle of the mess. Jeroboam does evil, and still the LORD saw that Israel's affliction was very bitter and "There was no one to help Israel," so He saved them by Jeroboam's hand (2 Kings 14:24-27). That rescue came because of the LORD's own compassion and His word, not because Jeroboam earned it. The word spoken to Jehu was fulfilled too (2 Kings 15:12). People keep wobbling, and God keeps His word.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery, baker. Judah's kings Azariah and Jotham did what was right, yet the high places stayed, and the people kept sacrificing and burning incense there (2 Kings 15:3-4, 34-35). Good is wonderful, but good with a leftover pile of old habits still has a catch. Ask the LORD to show you what you've been leaving standing, and then trust Him to bake you something new, because He is the One who says, "I am making all things new!" (Revelation 21:5).
